title: A Demonstration of Correlation of Correlation Analysis
text:
Introduction

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

import seaborn as sns

sns.set_context('talk')

df = sns.load_dataset('iris')

RQ: Does petal length predict petal width
To gain a better understanding of what the correlations might look like within the iris dataset from Seaborn, students are looking at . Our program will use this topic as a demonstration of working with correlation analysis in Python and Quarto; we have data from 150 flowers.


Literature Review


Methods
Given that we have two coloumns of continuous data (length of petal and width of petal measured in millimeters) we will evalute this relationship using simple correlation analysis and also a scatter plot. These two methods are classic and tradtional starting points when evaluting data like these


Results

corr_val = df['petal_length'].corr(df['petal_width'])

narative = "a very strong negative correaltion"

if corr_val > 0.8: 
    narrative = "a very strong positive correlation"
elif corr_val > .4:
    narrative = "a moderate postive correaltion"
elif corr_val > 0:
    narrative = "a positve but weak correlation"
elif corr_val > -.4:
    narrative = "a moderate negative correaltion"

Using the classic simple Pearson correlation approach these data produce a correltation coefficent of 0.9628654314027961, as such, given this result, we conclude that the relationship is a very strong positive correlation.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

#| label: fig-length-width-scatter
#| fig-cap: "A scatterplot of petal length and petal width"

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5))

sns.scatterplot(data = df, y = 'petal_length', x = 'petal_width')

plt.ylabel('Petal Length (mm)')
plt.xlabel('Petal Width (mm)')








As shown in ?@fig-length-width-scatter we set additional evidence of a strong positive correlation between an iris flower petal length and petal width
